borough: London Borough of Barking and Dagenham
decision_conditions: The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting, design, bulk and mass would be an undesirable addition to the existing dwelling. The cumulative impact of the proposal would cause undue harm to the character and appearance of the host terrace dwelling dwelling and prevailing form of development. This would result in a staggered roof form that would add significant bulk to the terrace dwelling and fails to mitigate impact to adjoining neighbours. The proposal is therefore contrary to the following policies which seek to ensure that development recognises local character and promotes good design:- National Planning Policy Framework National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, 2024)- Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021)- The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012)- Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037: (September 2024)

The proposed development, by reason of its scale, siting and design would cause severe harm to the neighbouring occupiers.  The proposed development fails to be appropriately setback from adjoining boundaries, and fails to mitigate any significant impact to the amenity of neighbouring dwellings. The proposed development would result in a significant level of overbearing, loss of outlook, loss of daylight, overlooking, and overshadowing to occur, therefore constituting unneighbourly development and contrary to:- National Planning Policy Framework National Planning Policy Framework (NPPF) (MHCLG, 2024)- Policy D4 of the London Plan (March 2021);- The Residential Extensions and Alterations Supplementary Planning Document (February 2012);- Policies SP2, DMD1 and DMD5 of The London Borough of Barking and Dagenham’s Local Plan 2037: (September 2024)
description: Construction of a part two storey part single storey rear extension
